messages:
ana: ran into a sharp router surge when applying ~150 flags across multiple tenants this morning. console apply was a single press and it fanout-ed everywhere. logs: 

ana: ```
[2026-03-23T12:03:02Z] apply-run: id=APPL-3001 user=ana scope=multi flags=148
[2026-03-23T12:03:03Z] orchestrator: batches=30 tasks=1480
[2026-03-23T12:03:04Z] router-us-east: queue_depth=940 capacity=1000 workers=95
[2026-03-23T12:03:05Z] quota-svc: throttle=true auto_pause=triggered
```

noah: ouch. was preview used?

ana: we ran preview but it only showed low risk due to sampling. the danger is cumulative small tenants with many outbound routes.

ops-bot: incident: router-us-east spike (INC-2026-03-23-011).

noah: proposal: add hysteresis to staged applies: instead of one-shot fanout, the orchestrator should do staggered windows with an inter-batch delay and dynamic reduction when pool metrics trend up. config keys: apply_hysteresis.batch_size (int), apply_hysteresis.delay_ms (int), apply_hysteresis.reduce_on_trend (bool).

tess: love hysteresis. also suggest estimator change to return a "burst_risk" metric that accounts for simultaneous pool touches. estimator API: POST /v1/apply/estimate -> {estimated_peak, burst_risk, suggested_hysteresis}.

noah: runtime plan: implement token-bucket + trend-based slow-down: if queue_depth increases >5% over 10s, pause between batches for an extra delay_ms and halve batch_size. emit telemetry apply.hysteresis.pauses and apply.hysteresis.adj_factor.

ana: UX: console should default to safe hysteresis for org-level templates and surface a small "one-click stagger" toggle on the final apply modal. also show the burst_risk score with simple explanation.

ops-bot: suggestion: auto-pause threshold remain at 80% capacity but hysteresis should aim to prevent hitting auto-pause.

tess: action items:
- noah: prototype hysteresis logic + telemetry (due 2026-03-27)
- ana: update preview to include burst_risk and suggested_hysteresis (due 2026-03-28)
- tess: console toggle + copy (due 2026-03-30)
- ops-bot: link incident INC-2026-03-23-011 and create CFG-934 ticket.

noah: question  should admin override exist? I'd prefer override only with explicit audit flag and a visible warning.

ana: agree. override requires apply_override=true and will be logged. default off for non-admins.

tess: ok linking CFG-934. will follow up once UI mock is ready. leaving thread open. :eyes:
